# Requirement test map

**Status:** Written 2026-09-14 against the register of the same day (190 requirements) and the applications as built on 2026-09-14
**Owner:** Matt Brown
**Source of the rows:** `00-overview/requirements.json` (generated by `build_register.py`, never hand-edited). The status column here is that register's status; where this map disagrees with what was found on screen it says so in the row and in section 3.
**System of record:** the ClickUp page under XMS 03 · Delivery. This file is the frozen copy (see the ClickUp Publication Map ruling of 2026-09-13).

## 1. How to read this document

One row per requirement. Four things per row:

| Column | What it holds |
|---|---|
| **Requirement** | The register id and title, and the register status: **Built**, **Partial**, **Not started** |
| **Where it lives** | The screen (internal desk path, or `/portal/...`), the API route, the worker job, or the data-layer rule that implements it. Internal paths are the route registry in `frontend/lib/routes.ts`; API routes are under `/v1` |
| **How to test** | Steps a person can follow on a running local stack to see the requirement working. Written for the seeded data (section 2). Where the requirement is enforced rather than shown, the step says what to try and what refusal to expect |
| **Gap** | Only where the register or this map found something missing; blank otherwise |

A **Not started** row says "Not built" and, where it helps, what the row will need. Those rows are kept so the map covers the whole register and the count of what is testable is honest.

Modules follow the register's module field. The seven revision 3 modules (Resolution Ladder through Outcomes) are all Not started and are listed at the end.

## 2. The stack a tester needs

| What | How |
|---|---|
| Database | `backend`: `pnpm db:up` (Postgres in Docker), then `pnpm db:migrate` |
| Seed | `backend`: `pnpm seed:dev` (two accounts, seven internal users, three portal users, 100 tickets per account; `SEED_TICKETS=20` for fewer) |
| API | `backend`: `pnpm start:dev` on port 3001 |
| Worker | `backend`: `pnpm start:worker:dev`. Needed for anything scheduled: SLA sweep and at-risk, container-case detection, renewal alerts, certification expiry, billing auto-lock, dashboard snapshots, report schedules, outbox delivery (email, webhooks, finance) |
| MCP | `backend`: `pnpm start:mcp:dev`, or the same routes inside the API under `/mcp` |
| ServiceNow stand-in | `backend`: `pnpm standin` (port 3005, `STANDIN_PORT` to change). The Table API subset the connector uses, with auto-echo and fault injection |
| Desk | `frontend`: `pnpm dev` on port 3000, `NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_DEV_MODE=true` on the local target |
| Sign in (desk) | `/dev/sign-in` lists every seeded user; pick one. Or `pnpm dev:token --email <email>` in `backend` and paste |
| Sign in (portal) | `/portal/sign-in`, same dev token flow for a portal user |

Seeded identities (all `@example.test`):

| Who | Role | Use them for |
|---|---|---|
| `admin` | Administrator | Everything under `/admin`, configuration, audit, migration |
| `ana.costa`, `ben.okafor` | Consultant, OneStream Technical group | Working tickets, logging time, the timesheet |
| `chloe.martin` | Consultant, Infrastructure group | A second group for routing and group-queue tests |
| `dev.patel` | Dispatcher, CSM group | Dispatch, assignment, bulk actions |
| `erin.walsh` | Account Owner, CSM group | Scope decisions, contracts, budgets, report packs |
| `femi.adeyemi` | Finance | Billing periods, exports, the finance connector |
| Pat Client | Portal, Requester | The client's view: one account, own requests |
| Sam Owner | Portal, Account Admin | Org-wide requests (`portal:view-org-tickets`) |
| Robin Reader | Portal, Read Only | What a reader cannot do |

Accounts: **BRK** (Brookfield) and **AUS** (Austral Mining). Each has contracts, rate cards, a calendar, demand lines and tickets. Where a step says "the other account", it means the one the signed-in user is not looking at.

Two rules that apply to every row:

1. **The server decides.** Every step that says "refused" means the API answered 403, 404 or 409 and the screen worded it. Nothing below is proven by a control being hidden; hidden controls are a mirror of the server's decision, not the decision.
2. **Every mutation is on the Activity tab and in `/admin/audit`.** Any row that changes data can be double-checked there; the map does not repeat that on each row.

## 3. What mapping found

Rows the register calls Built that a tester will find thinner than the title suggests, found while writing the steps below. None of these changes the register; they are recorded here so the next person does not rediscover them.

| Requirement | What was found |
|---|---|
| TB-10 Per-ticket hours breakdown | The Time tab shows the breakdown; there is no Export on it. The hours reach a file only through the billing period export (TB-14). The Budget tab's own entry export is disabled until an export route exists |
| CAP-09 On-call rota | The register says a rota exists in the backend. No table, domain rule or module named rota, on-call or shift was found on 2026-09-14; treat it as Not started until someone points at the code |
| DR-01 Near-real-time refresh | The Operations dashboard polls every 60 seconds; there is no push. That meets "defined refresh interval" and does not meet "push updates" |
| AI-08 to AI-13 (the six Built AI rows) | Every one is built as a guard or a record, not as a visible suggestion, because the harness is unconfigured. They are testable through the switch, the MCP gate and the audit stream, and that is what the steps below do |
| DM-04 Parallel run period | Not started as a feature; the mechanism it needs, one-way ingest (SN-09), exists. Nothing more is likely to be built for it |
| CP-01 SSO via SAML/OIDC | The portal signs in through Clerk when configured. There is no per-client IdP federation and no local-account fallback distinct from it |

Change the map and activate again: the versions tab lists both; no code changed | |
